title: Constructions & loci
examples: How do I find the bisector of an angle?
What is the locus of points that are always three centimeters from a point?
If I shade a region, what am I actually showing?

explain.say: Today we learn about bisectors and loci. A bisector splits an angle exactly in half. We can use a compass and ruler to draw this line.
To bisect an angle, first draw an arc from the vertex. Next, draw arcs from both sides that meet in two points. Finally, draw a line through those two points.

items: Draw an arc from the vertex.
Draw arcs from both sides meeting.
Draw a line through the two points.

explain.say: The locus is the set of all points that follow a rule. If the rule is being equally distant from two points, the locus is a straight line.

items: Equidistant from two points: straight line

explain.say: For a locus equidistant from two points, you draw the perpendicular bisector. This line is exactly halfway between the two given points.
Shading a region means showing all the points that meet a certain condition. For example, shading all points closer to line A than line B.

items: Closer to line A than line B

faq.q: What is the difference between a bisector and a perpendicular bisector?
faq.a: A bisector splits an angle into two equal parts. A perpendicular bisector splits a line segment into two equal parts at a right angle.
asks: How do I split an angle in half?
What is the line that cuts a segment in half?

faq.q: Does the locus always have to be a straight line?
faq.a: No, the locus can be a curve, like a circle, depending on the rule. For example, the locus of points equidistant from a point is a circle.
asks: Can the set of points be curved?
What shape is the locus of points a fixed distance away?

faq.q: If I shade a region, am I drawing a boundary?
faq.a: No, shading shows the area where the condition is true. The boundary itself is usually the line that separates the 'yes' area from the 'no' area.
asks: Is the line I draw the boundary?
What does shading represent in geometry?

faq.q: Can I find the locus of points equidistant from three points?
faq.a: Finding the locus from three points is complex. You would typically find the intersection of the three perpendicular bisectors of the sides of the triangle formed.
asks: What if I use three points?
How do I find the center point related to three points?

faq.q: Do I need a compass for all these constructions?
faq.a: Yes, a compass is very useful for drawing arcs needed for bisectors and finding points at a fixed distance. A ruler is also necessary.
asks: What tools do I need for these constructions?

facts: A bisector divides an angle into two equal angles.
The locus of points equidistant from two points is their perpendicular bisector.
The locus of points equidistant from a single point forms a circle.
Shading shows all points satisfying a given geometric condition.

quiz.say: To find the locus of points that are the same distance from two fixed points, you draw:

options.show: A line parallel to the points
options.say: A line parallel to the points

options.show: A circle passing through the points
options.say: A circle passing through the points

quiz.why: The perpendicular bisector is the line exactly halfway between the two points, meaning all points on it are equally distant.

wrong.0: Parallel lines do not guarantee equal distance from two specific points.
wrong.2: This is used for angles, not for two separate points.
wrong.3: A circle would only work if the points were the same distance from the center.

quiz.say: If you shade the region containing all points closer to line A than line B, what line forms the boundary of your shade?

options.show: The line equidistant from A and B
options.say: The line equidistant from A and B

quiz.why: The boundary is the set of points that are exactly the same distance from both line A and line B.

wrong.1: Line A is only one of the two reference lines, not the dividing line.
wrong.2: Similarly, Line B is not the dividing boundary.
wrong.3: The boundary line must be defined by the equal distance rule, not just perpendicularity.

quiz.say: Which construction is used to find the line that cuts an angle into two equal halves?

options.show: Drawing a circle through the vertex
options.say: Drawing a circle through the vertex

options.show: Drawing a line parallel to the sides
options.say: Drawing a line parallel to the sides

quiz.why: The angle bisector construction is the specific method taught for dividing an angle into two equal parts.

wrong.0: This method is for dividing a line segment, not an angle.
wrong.1: This action does not guarantee the equal division of the angle.
wrong.2: Parallel lines do not relate to the equal division of an angle.
